preamble: Monophthongization is a sound change where a diphthong simplifies into a single, stable vowel sound. This process often reduces articulatory effort and can be found in the historical development of languages like French and various dialects of English.

examples.note: Hui is noted for massive loss of codas, including -i, -u and nasals.
Middle Indo-Aryan monophthongization of au to o (and ai to e)
au > open [ɔː] (Late Middle Japanese) > [oː]; the open/close long-o distinction merged in the Edo period

sources: Ladefoged, P. (2001). A Course in Phonetics.
Wells, J. C. (1982). Accents of English.
Masica, C. P. (1991). The Indo-Aryan Languages. Cambridge University Press.
Frellesvig, B. (2010). A History of the Japanese Language. Cambridge University Press.
